court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: XV Additional Sessions Judge, Chennai (C.A.No.80 of 2015); XV Metropolitan Magistrate, George Town, Chennai (DVC.No.23 of 2013)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: S.Selvakumar, husband; S.Kalaivani, wife; S.Senthil, son; S.Sentamil, daughter — Petitioners

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The wife had filed a petition before the learned XV Metropolitan Magistrate, Chennai in DVC.No.23 of 2013. The order passed by the learned XV Metropolitan Magistrate, Chennai in Domestic Violence Case No.23 of 2013 was confirmed by the learned XV Additional Sessions Judge, City Civil Court by Judgment dated 03.08.2015. The petitioners are seeking to set aside this judgment.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the complainant to prove that the marriage was valid and not a sham.
legal_principles.held: The claim of the complainant that she is the wife of the first Respondent is also denied. The claim is made based on marriage performed under threat and duress by the Police Officials, Kothavalchavadi which is not a recognized marriage.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

legal_principles.principle: A marriage performed under threat and duress is not a recognized marriage.
legal_principles.held: The claim made by the complainant that the first Respondent approached the brother of the complainant/B.Nagaraj to marry the complainant which was also resisted by her brother as they hail from different community, Finally, B.Nagaraj agreed to solemnize the marriage only with the permission of the parents of the first Respondent.

outcome.final_order: The court directed the respondent to rent out a house and pay monthly rent for the complainant, or accommodate the complainant if the respondent has their own house. The respondent was also directed to pay Rs.5,000/- per month towards maintenance.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
